name: Dhuska
subtitle: jharkhandi deep-fried rice and chana dal discs, crisp outside and soft within
prepNotes: Soak the rice and chana dal together in plenty of water for at least 5 hours or overnight; they must crush easily between your nails before you grind.
Grind the batter at least 2 hours before frying and leave it at room temperature — it does not ferment, but resting makes the dhuska lighter.
Do not add extra water to the batter at the last minute; a slack batter drinks oil.

steps.text: Drain the soaked rice and dal thoroughly, shaking the colander dry.
Grind them with the ginger, green chillies and 150 ml water into a thick, slightly grainy batter — the texture of idli batter, not smooth.
steps.tip: Add the water in stages. Too thin and the dhuska will not hold its shape in the oil.

steps.text: Beat in the turmeric, chilli powder, cumin seeds and salt, then rest the batter 2 hours covered.
Stir in the coriander leaves and whisk the batter hard for 30 seconds to aerate it.
Heat the oil in a kadhai to 180C — a drop of batter should rise and sizzle within 3 seconds.
steps.tip: Too cool and they turn greasy; too hot and the centres stay raw.

steps.text: Slide in ladlefuls of batter, 3 at a time, easing each one into a rough 10cm disc as it hits the oil.
Fry 2 minutes until they puff and float, then turn and fry another 2 to 3 minutes until deep gold and crisp at the edges.
steps.tip: Wait for them to float before turning, or they collapse.

steps.text: Lift onto a rack, not paper, so the undersides stay crisp, and repeat with the rest of the batter.
Serve hot with ghugni or aloo chokha.

storage: Best eaten within the hour. Leftovers keep 1 day refrigerated; crisp them up in a hot oven or a dry pan for 4 minutes rather than the microwave.
